canonical_statement: Let (Omega, F, mu) be a probability space and let (X_n) be an independent, identically distributed sequence of measurable random variables with values in a measurable space E. If a measurable path event A in E^Nat is invariant under every finite-support permutation of the coordinates, then mu({omega | (n |-> X_n(omega)) belongs to A}) is zero or one.
domain_and_universes: Provisional universes u v; Omega : Type u and E : Type v with measurable spaces; mu : Measure Omega; X : Nat -> Omega -> E; A : Set (Nat -> E). Exact typeclass ordering remains open.
ordered_binders: mu : Measure Omega with IsProbabilityMeasure mu
hypotheses: the coordinate maps X_n are jointly represented by the measurable sequence path map
the family X is mutually independent under mu
all coordinates have the same distribution under mu
A is measurable in the sequence-space product measurable structure
A is invariant under every finite-support permutation of Nat
conclusion: mu (processPath X preimage A) = 0 or mu (processPath X preimage A) = 1
